title: The square isomorphism is the identity on underlying objects
statement:
For every $S_X$-module $M$, the component at $M$ of the isomorphism of
[def-sfb-comap-mapmod-square] has underlying morphism the identity of $F(M)$.

proof.text: First compute the scalar-restriction comparisons from [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. For monoid morphisms $a:A\to B$, $b:B\to T$ and a $T$-module $N$ with action $\gamma_N$, restriction successively along $b$ and $a$ gives the action $\gamma_N\circ(b\otimes 1_N)\circ(a\otimes 1_N)=\gamma_N\circ((b\circ a)\otimes 1_N)$. This is exactly restriction along $b\circ a$ by functoriality of tensor. Equal scalar morphisms also give equal actions. In each case the canonical comparison and its inverse have underlying map $1_N$: the module-morphism equation of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] reduces to equality of these actions. Naturality reduces to $u\circ1=1\circ u$, since restriction leaves every underlying arrow unchanged. Functor-composition associators likewise evaluate to identity module maps, since reparenthesizing functor composition changes neither its object nor arrow assignment.

proof.text: Next compute compatibility of transport with restriction, using the action formula of [def-sfb-modobj-transport] and [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. Write $m$ for the underlying object of the given $S_X$-module $M$ and $\gamma:S_X\otimes m\to m$ for its action. The $FR_X$-actions on transport after restriction and on restriction after transport are respectively $F(\gamma\circ(\varphi_X\otimes1_m))\circ\mu^F_{R_X,m}$ and $F\gamma\circ\mu^F_{S_X,m}\circ(F\varphi_X\otimes1_{Fm})$. They are equal, because $F$ preserves composition and the naturality axiom of its lax monoidal structure says $F(\varphi_X\otimes1_m)\circ\mu^F_{R_X,m}=\mu^F_{S_X,m}\circ(F\varphi_X\otimes1_{Fm})$. Thus $1_{Fm}$ is linear in both directions by [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. These identity maps give the canonical comparison and its inverse; naturality reduces to $Fu\circ1=1\circ Fu$, since both functors take an underlying module map $u$ to $Fu$. No structure map $\mu^F$ is inverted.

proof.text:
Use the specified common-composite comparison of [def-sfb-comap-mapmod-square]. Write $T_S$ and $T_R$ for $\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ on $S_X$-modules and $R_X$-modules respectively. Up to the functor-composition associators, its path is
$$
\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi_Y}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_S}\circ T_S
\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_S\circ\varphi_Y}\circ T_S
\cong\operatorname{Res}_{F\varphi_X\circ\eta_R}\circ T_S
\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_R}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{F\varphi_X}\circ T_S
\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_R}\circ T_R\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi_X}.
$$
The first and third comparisons are the composition comparisons of step 1; the second is its equal-morphism comparison applied to $\eta_S\circ\varphi_Y=F\varphi_X\circ\eta_R$; the fourth is the inverse of step 2, followed by $\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_R}$. Each constituent and each functor associator has underlying identity at $M$, by steps 1 and 2. Whiskering preserves this property: restriction leaves underlying arrows unchanged by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], and transport sends an identity to $F(1_m)=1_{Fm}$ by [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. Composition of module morphisms is composition in the ambient category by [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Thus the specified square isomorphism has underlying component a composite of identities of $Fm$, hence $1_{Fm}$, as required.
